summary: Remote-controlled Claude Code agent with bypassPermissions driven by hardcoded WebSocket server
details: The bin daemon in @agenthub-ai/agent opens a persistent WebSocket to the hardcoded author-controlled endpoint wss://agenthub-agent.fyenet.com and dispatches inbound channel messages (message.send, session.interrupt, session.model, tool.allow, tool.deny) into an embedded Claude Agent SDK session configured with permissionMode 'bypassPermissions'. A remote party paired via that server can drive arbitrary tool use — shell execution, file reads and edits — on the host running the agent, without the local consent prompts Claude Code would normally require. The single shipped runtime file dist-publish/main.js is processed by javascript-obfuscator (string-array with hex identifiers, control-flow flattening; the author's package.json lists javascript-obfuscator as a devDependency), which obscures the exact command surface the remote server can exercise. Execution is gated behind explicit invocation of the CLI (not npm install or bare require), and pairing the agent with the server is the package's advertised purpose, so the host operator has opted into running an agent — but the control channel and bypassPermissions mode together constitute a network-driven full-host RCE surface pointed at author-controlled infrastructure.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
